answer:
**Answer:** Both default to waiting for a new frame. For **IMAQdx Get Image2.vi**, 'Buffer Number Mode' defaults to **Next**. For **IMAQdx Grab2.vi**, 'Wait for Next Buffer?' defaults to **TRUE**. A display loop slower than the camera therefore shows recent frames and silently skips the ones in between. It does not work through every frame or build up a lag.

**1. Get Image2 'Buffer Number Mode' is Next.** NI's reference page for Get Image2 says the default is Next, meaning the driver waits for the next acquired buffer. Wiring 'Buffer Number In' is optional in that mode.
- https://www.ni.com/docs/en-US/bundle/ni-imaqdx-vi-ref/page/ni-imaqdx_vi_reference/imaqdx_get_image2.html
- Caveat: this page loads its content with JavaScript, so my fetch came back empty. The "default is Next" wording came from the search engine's copy of that page, not a page I read directly.

**2. Grab2 'Wait for Next Buffer?' is TRUE.** NI forum users say that with TRUE (the default) Grab waits for the next buffer to be ready. With FALSE it returns the last buffer already acquired.
- https://forums.ni.com/t5/LabVIEW/Quick-question-about-grab-function-in-IMAQdx/td-p/3607125
- https://natinst.public.imaq.general.narkive.com/4VcvjWY5/imaqdx-grab-in-a-while-loop
- Caveat: NI's own Grab2 page (https://www.ni.com/docs/en-US/bundle/ni-imaqdx-vi-ref/page/ni-imaqdx_vi_reference/imaqdx_grab2.html) also failed to load. So this default rests on forum posts, not NI's documentation.

**3. What this means for a slow display loop:**
- **Each call waits for a new frame.** An NI staff member explains "Next" with an example: if you last got buffer 5 and the camera has reached buffer 10, the driver waits for buffer 11 (https://forums.ni.com/t5/Machine-Vision/Buffer-Mode-quot-Next-quot-and-quot-Every-quot-in-IMAQdx-Extract/td-p/4079556). That thread is about the NXG "Extract Image" function, which uses the same buffer modes. I'm assuming LabVIEW's Get Image2 behaves the same way.
- **Frames in between are skipped without warning.** The loop never catches up on older frames, and no error is raised. On a fast camera, each call can also block for up to one frame period.
- **Old buffers get overwritten.** The camera fills a ring of buffers, and a slow reader's old buffers are overwritten. When a requested buffer is gone, the driver by default hands back the newest valid one. It can instead be set to hand back the oldest valid one or to raise an error.
  - https://documentation.help/NI-IMAQdx/buffer_management.html (returned 403 when fetched; I only saw a search snippet)
  - https://forums.ni.com/t5/Machine-Vision/Trying-to-understand-how-the-buffers-work-in-Imaqdx-aquisition/td-p/3986038
  - https://forums.ni.com/t5/LabVIEW/Buffers-output-in-IMAQdx/td-p/3644259
- **How to detect or prevent dropped frames:** Compare the 'Buffer Number Out' of successive calls to count how many frames were skipped (first Grab thread above). If you need every frame, NI staff recommend "Every" mode with the Overwrite Mode setting on "Fail", so dropped frames raise an error (thread 3986038 above).

**What isn't settled:** I couldn't read NI's official pages for either VI or for Buffer Management, and I couldn't open the NI article comparing "Last" and "Last New" (https://knowledge.ni.com/KnowledgeArticleDetails?id=kA03q000001DwvoCAC&l=en-US; certificate error). The defaults are consistent across the sources above, but they come from search snippets and forum posts, not NI pages I read in full. Checking the input's default in LabVIEW's Context Help would confirm them.
